title: I Took the Dyeing-Vat Reservation to the Chair Who Left My Fiber in the Bath

parts.text: I lifted the lid at vat four at 11:03 a.m. and chair Saffron was already stirring my numbered fiber. The slate said: ONE VAT. THREE HOURS. FIBER STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-two, dye studio member, holding a recipe that listed our mordant. Saffron shrugged. "Chairs are the bath." I photographed the slate, the booking, and her tongs on my skein. Then I asked for the vat log. At 11:11 the studio pinged why Saffron's name was on my fiber. I kept my voice steam-soft and let the timestamp talk. A slate is only a slate until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Saffron's tongs on my skein during our booking.

social.video_title: She stirred my numbered fiber in my bath — Part 1/2
social.description: Dye vat, a chair on my skein, a three-hour slate she posted. I logged the tongs. Would you have asked for the vat log?

parts.text: Saffron called it a dip until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the slate, and the tongs still. The fiber went back to my pot. Saffron ran her own three hours and told the next chair atmosphere was always about take. Take is a word chairs use when a booking exists. Vat policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE BATH. I keep our recipe on a labeled clip. Saffron brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the bath — Part 2/2
social.description: Vat log, numbered fiber, and a second line on the slate. Was a dip ever my skein?
